question: **Fill in the blank**: The Factory Act 1881 primarily regulated ____.

options.text: working hours of women and children
night shifts hours for men only
minimum wage for women and children

solution:
The correct answer is __**working hours of women and children**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Factory Act of 1881** was introduced during British rule in India to regulate working conditions in factories, particularly focusing on the **working hours of women and children**.
 
• The Act limited the number of working hours for children under the age of **12** to **9 hours per day**, aiming to prevent exploitation and ensure their welfare.
 
• It also mandated that children working in factories were to receive **four holidays in a month** and adequate rest intervals during work hours.
 
• For women, the Act aimed to regulate working hours to ensure they were not subjected to long or harsh working hours, which could negatively impact their health and family responsibilities.
 
• The Factory Act of 1881 was significant because it marked the beginning of **legislative efforts** to regulate labor conditions in India, paving the way for future labor reforms. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Important Provisions of Factory Act 1881:**

 
 
• The Act was introduced by the British government as a response to social reform efforts aimed at improving labor conditions.
 
• It was applicable to factories employing **100 or more workers**, focusing on industries where exploitation of labor was rampant.
 
• The Act mandated the provision of **ventilation, lighting, and sanitary conditions** in factories to improve worker health.
 
• It required factory owners to maintain **records of child workers** to ensure compliance with age and working hour restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Developments:**
 
 
• The **Factory Act of 1891** further enhanced the provisions of the 1881 Act by reducing working hours for children and introducing restrictions on night work for women.
 
• Later, the **Indian Factories Act of 1948** replaced earlier legislations and introduced comprehensive measures for labor welfare, including safety, working conditions, and health regulations.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Labor Welfare:**
 
 
• The Factory Act of 1881 was the first step toward improving labor conditions in India, though its scope was limited to specific industries and regions.
 
• It raised awareness of the need for **labor laws** in India and led to increased focus on worker rights and welfare in subsequent decades.
 
 
 
• **Similar Laws in Other Countries:**
 
 
• In England, the **Factory Acts** of the 19th century aimed to improve working conditions, especially for women and children, setting an example for India.
 
• Other countries, such as the United States, also passed labor laws during the Industrial Revolution to regulate working hours and ensure safety in factories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The Factory Act of 1881 was introduced during the tenure of **Lord Ripon**, who is known for his reform-oriented policies in India.
 
• **Age Restrictions:** The Act defined a child worker as someone under the age of **12 years**, marking an early attempt to regulate child labor.
 
• **Industrial Revolution Influence:** The Act was inspired by similar labor laws enacted in Britain during the **Industrial Revolution**.
 
• **Social Impact:** While the Act was limited in scope, it marked an important step toward addressing labor exploitation and improving working conditions in colonial India.
